whatItIs.statement: Displays a button or a component that looks like a button.

whenToUse.statement: Use a button when the control triggers an action or event, such as submitting a form, opening a dialog, cancelling an action, or deleting an item.

whenNotToUse.statement: Do not use a button for navigation; match the visual treatment and role to the link function.

howToUse.statement: For a link-shaped navigation control, use the buttonVariants helper with a plain link element instead of Button.
Give the button an accessible label; text content is the default accessible name.

To announce the result of a Button action, such as Logging in… or Login failed, render a caller-controlled <Status> (or <Status variant="error"> for an important failure) next to the Button; Button loading itself announces nothing. Keep the Status mounted and change its children.
Inside a Form, use <Button type="submit"> for the submit action. A native button with no type inside a form submits it, so give every other Button, such as Cancel or a toggle, type="button".

options.statement: Use the size option to change the size of the button.
When placing an icon before or after the label, use the documented icon-position marker so the component can apply the corresponding spacing.

Use the loading prop to show that the action the button triggers is in progress, for example <Button loading>Log in</Button>. While loading, Button renders the Spinner before the label, sets aria-busy="true", and disables the native button so it cannot be activated again by pointer, keyboard, or form submit. The caller controls the state: Button does not run or track async work, so set loading back to false when the work ends. Loading has no effect when asChild is true.

writing.statement: Keep a toggle button's label unchanged when its pressed state changes.

Keep the label unchanged while loading, so Log in stays Log in rather than becoming Loading…. The Spinner is hidden from assistive technology and aria-busy conveys the busy state, which keeps the accessible name the action name. Loading does not announce the result, so report success or failure with a separate status or alert message.

guidance.statement: When the element navigates rather than triggers an action, use a link.
